findings.title: Rightful distribution and seedlike scattering

Its seed-scattering image makes waste appear as material dispersed away from the claims that give it a destination; the wider resource sequence also places that flow between immobilized restraint and unmeasured release.

The preceding instruction names recipients and an owned right; the following hand images and changing provision add limits to the flow. Brotherhood then meets the claimant relation as a protected tie, while the Satan/Rabb clause connects wasteful affiliation with denial of the gift's source.

The packet's distance-from-good facet for shatan is an associated derivational explanation, not an established etymology or the focus noun's sole meaning. findings.title: Wealth held inside answerable claims
findings.claim: The orphan-wealth and just-measure instructions make a useful context for the focus: an apparent holder can be understood as a custodian inside another's vulnerable claim, covenant, and measure. Tabdhir then breaches answerable custody rather than wasting something assumed to be simply one's own.
findings.mechanism: The focus waste carrier and Rabb's nurture-to-completion branch meet the orphan's wealth, the requirement to fulfill a covenant, and straight measure. Those separate obligations contact the focus and change the model of possession into care that must preserve another's future and remain answerable.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's resource warning can be seen as a question of stewardship under claims and public measure, not only private preference.
findings.containment: The unified custody model is an attributed synthesis; the orphan-property, covenant, and measurement rules may also be separate legal cases. The focus does not by itself state that every asset is held in trust.

epistemic.reason: Every named context coordinate agrees with the supplied surfaces, while the single custody model is an attributed synthesis from a legacy-unbound HFT record.

findings.title: Information as an entrusted flow
findings.claim: As an exploratory second register, the focus form can carry the supplied branch of spreading secrets or reports. The speech restraint in 17:23 and the knowledge, hearing, following, and accountability limits in 17:36 frame information as a flow that must be governed rather than scattered.
findings.mechanism: The focus's mubadhdhirin carrier meets the exact speech and faculty references in the pericope; kafur's covering image adds an attributed contrast between releasing what should be held and concealing received benefit. This contact extends the focus beyond fiscal flow without displacing its immediate resource reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The same dispersal image can be considered for speech and received information, where knowledge and accountability constrain transmission.
findings.containment: The immediate clause and neighboring 17:26 instruction remain fiscal. 17:23 regulates speech to parents, while 17:36 prohibits following what lacks knowledge and makes faculties answerable; neither explicitly accuses anyone of spreading a secret. The HFT's accusation and public-repute descriptions remain attributed applications, and the alternative that the branch is inactive in this fiscal construction remains live.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is registered and every HFT coordinate matches its context surface, but the move from regulated speech and perception to informational dissipation is an exploratory attributed inference.

findings.title: Practical allegiance in the closing frame

That contact shifts the focus from an isolated spending warning toward a test of which order ordinary practice embodies.
findings.reader_payoff: A routine allocation decision can be perceived as participation in a wider ethical allegiance.
findings.containment: This is a legacy-unbound HFT synthesis. The closing verses may summarize separate commands without recasting each violation as rival worship; the finding does not say that spending alone constitutes formal polytheism.

epistemic.reason: The trace coordinates match the supplied closing ayat, but construing the listed economic practice as lived allegiance is an attributed theological inference.

findings.title: Ingratitude against praise of the Lord
findings.claim: The focus's intensive ingratitude to its Rabb forms a specific counter-response to 1:2's praise of Allah as Lord of the worlds. The external ayah adds a positive, universal praise response to the focus's local description of denial.
findings.mechanism: The focus Rabb and kafur carriers meet the separate hamd phrase in 1:2, whose supplied text joins praise to Allah and Rabb al-alamin. Their contact changes the ingratitude clause into an inversion of praise directed to the same Lord.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's failure of gratitude can be heard against a voiced alternative of praise for the sustaining Lord.
findings.containment: This is an inferred comparison between two supplied ayat, not evidence that 17:27 quotes or intentionally alludes to 1:2. The native pericope already supplies worship and mercy; the external praise contributes only this counter-response.

epistemic.reason: The exact external phrase and focus carriers are supplied, while their inter-ayah contrast is an interpretive inference.

findings.containment: This is an external contextual inference from the individual ayah 1:4, not a whole-surah frame or a claim that 17:27 names the Day of Recompense. Native 17:34-35 already supplies immediate custody and measure; the overlay adds only the future horizon.

epistemic.reason: The focus and individual external trigger are exact, but connecting their ownership and resource relations to future recompense is inferential.

friction_notes: The counter-kinship trace's 17:24 word-11 surface and root agree as ر ب و, but its cited root_000537/B005 record maps to ر ب ب. That exact branch reference is excluded; the independently registered focus Rabb-nurture branch remains activated by the upbringing context.

All eight HFT records are legacy_unbound. Their valid contextual traces are retained as attributed evidence, with the child-killing, authority, information-flow, and closing-allegiance extensions bounded by their stated alternatives.
The 1:2 praise contrast and 1:4 recompense horizon are external overlays inferred from the individually supplied ayat; neither establishes intentional cross-text reference.
